title: Oracle: rulings and handoff (BL-14)
body:
Oracle ruling on the logged evidence `BL-14`, dispatched by the unattended delivery driver.

**OD-13** — the owner's 2026-08-19 ruling overrules OD-5 on the whole-transcript cap, so this decision supersedes `R1001` and adds `R1008`.

- `R1001` is retired. The merged plan `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md` implements it in all three slices, so it is superseded and must not be built as merged.
- `R1008` keeps the reporting half of `R1001`: the checkpoint projection reports, per routing path, how many videos took it and the characters and projected tokens it accounts for, plus the bundle count for each whole-transcript video delivered across sequential bundles.
- `OD-4`/`R1000` is untouched, and its re-cut (`docs/plans/oracle/recut-merged-excerpts.md`) still lands first: the ratio only routes honestly once each transcript character is counted once.

The handoff at `docs/oracle/handoff-2026-08-20-1.md` carries the steward's next step — re-cut the superseded plan against `OD-13`, covering `R28` and `R1008`, with two routing paths rather than three.

Opened by the server-side `open-pr` workflow at the driver's request: this session cannot mint App identity (the hosted platform's proxy owns the credential), and a pipeline pull request authored by the owner would hollow out `owner-authored.sh`.
